_what: THE BATTERY THE WORD SHELVES EXIST TO ANSWER — the missing denominator.
_why: On the 68-question weave battery the engine serves a lexicon/etymology/dictionary card as the
LEADING source on 12 questions, and ask.py's own 0-FP word-intent detectors fire on ZERO of
them. So any rule of the form 'a word card may not lead unless the question asks about words'
scores 12/12 on that battery while saying NOTHING about the case the shelves exist for.
That is the same error as reading the exact-title boost's 0-of-68 as a clean bill (2026-11-17):
a zero without its denominator is uninterpretable. This file is the denominator.
WRITTEN BEFORE ANY RULE WAS BUILT, deliberately, so it cannot be fitted to the rule it grades.
Phrasings are drawn from the engine's OWN documented cases where they exist (ask.py names
'what does agape mean', 'how do you pronounce Nebuchadnezzar', 'what part of speech is
quickly'), plus the plain ways a reader actually asks. Several are deliberately phrased so the
0-FP router MISSES them ('show me the original Greek word', 'what is the Hebrew behind...') —
a precision router and a permissive gate have opposite failure modes, and the gate must be
graded on the phrasings the router was built to let through.
_expect: shelf_in: the shelves any of which is a RIGHT leader for this question.
